To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the overlap operator can be solved with a precision of 10−8 at a cost of 30–100 times that of a TM operator, (ii) the cost of a TM operator can be reduced by a factor of about 10–20 using a combination of even–odd preconditioning and adaptive precision, (iii) the cost of the overlap operator can also be reduced by a similar factor using low-mode preconditioning and adaptive precison, (iv) the cost of
the overlap fermion algorithm is by a factor of about 50 more expensive than the TM algorithm.
overlap fermions are by a factor 30–120 slower than TM fermions, and that low-mode preconditioning can speed up overlap fermion calculations by a factor of two to three.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of the computational cost of the overlap operator with the cost of the TM operator in the calculation of hadron correlation functions.
the development and comparison of iterative methods for solving linear systems of equations in the overlap and TM formalism.
the question of whether the use of overlap fermions in lattice QCD is a viable alternative to the use of Wilson-type fermions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the current state-of-the-art, the TM formulation is the method of choice for the generation of gauge configurations with dynamical quarks.
the twisted mass formulation is a better choice for simulations at physical pion masses.
the overlap operator is more expensive to invert, but the TM operator is more expensive in terms of computer resources to set up and store.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the range of pion masses studied here, the TM formulation of lattice QCD appears to be a very promising approach for the study of hadrons with light quarks.
the TM formulation is the best choice for the study of hadron structure and spectroscopy.
the TM fermion operator is more expensive than the overlap operator, but the latter is more expensive than one may naively expect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost per unit of accuracy is much smaller for TM fermions than for the overlap operator.
the overlap operator is not a viable alternative to TM fermions for large-scale simulations.
the overlap operator is a very expensive computational object, even when using the best possible solvers.
